title: Time management
examples: How do I plan my week to fit in everything?
What is the best way to group similar tasks together?
Can batching really save me time?

explain.say: Today we are looking at better ways to manage your time.

items: Goal setting: define what needs to be done
Prioritizing: decide what is most important first
Scheduling: allocate specific time slots for tasks

explain.say: Planning involves looking ahead to organize your work ahead of time.
A concrete example is breaking a big project into small daily steps.
Next we will explore task batching to improve focus and efficiency.
Batching means grouping similar activities together and doing them all at once.
In real life, you can batch your errands to save travel time.

faq.q: How often should I plan my work week?
faq.a: It is best to plan your week every Sunday evening. This gives you a clear map for the coming days. You could also plan daily or weekly depending on your workload.
asks: When should I sit down to plan?
How often is enough time planning?

faq.q: What is the difference between planning and scheduling?
faq.a: Planning is deciding what needs to be done. Scheduling is putting those tasks onto a specific calendar time. Think of it as deciding the route versus setting the departure time.
asks: Do I plan first or schedule first?

faq.q: Can batching work for creative tasks?
faq.a: Yes, you can batch creative tasks like writing or brainstorming. Set aside a dedicated block just for deep creative work. This prevents context switching.

faq.q: If I get interrupted, does it ruin my batching?
faq.a: Frequent interruptions make batching very difficult. Try to block out specific times for deep work when you will not be disturbed. Communicate your focus time to others.
asks: How do I protect my focus time?

faq.q: What if I have too many things to plan?
faq.a: Start by identifying your top three most important goals for the week. Focus your planning energy on those key items first. Everything else can wait until those are complete.
asks: Where do I start when everything is urgent?
How do I prioritize when everything matters?

facts: Planning helps you visualize the path to a large goal.
Batching reduces context switching, which saves mental energy.
Prioritization means identifying the most critical tasks first.
A good plan should be flexible enough to adjust to changes.

quiz.say: You have to write a report, answer emails, and attend a meeting. Which technique is best for grouping the emails together?
quiz.why: Batching groups similar tasks, like all emails, together for focused work.

wrong.0: Planning is about deciding what to do, not grouping the actual work.
wrong.1: Prioritizing tells you which task is most important, not how to group them.
wrong.2: Scheduling puts the tasks on a calendar, but doesn't describe the grouping method.

quiz.say: If you dedicate one hour solely to answering all your emails, what skill are you demonstrating?
quiz.why: This is a perfect example of batching, keeping all similar activities together.

wrong.1: Planning would be deciding that emails need to be done that hour.
wrong.2: Prioritizing would be deciding if emails are more important than the meeting.
wrong.3: Scheduling would be writing 'Email Time' on your calendar.

quiz.say: What is the main benefit of breaking a large project into small steps?

options.show: It makes the work feel less overwhelming.
options.say: It makes the work feel less overwhelming.

options.show: It guarantees you will finish early.
options.say: It guarantees you will finish early.

options.show: It eliminates the need for focus.
options.say: It eliminates the need for focus.

quiz.why: Small steps create manageable chunks, reducing feelings of being overwhelmed.

wrong.1: Breaking tasks down helps with pacing, but external delays can still happen.
wrong.2: You still need to plan when you will do those small steps.
wrong.3: Focus is still required for each small step to be completed well.
